definition_zh: 第八十；八十分之一；八十岁生日
definition_en: the eightieth in order, one of eighty equal parts, or the eightieth birthday of someone
core_image: 桌上插满细蜡烛，蛋糕几乎被烛光盖住
scene: 全村人挤进小屋，为老人过第八十个生日。The whole village came to her eightieth birthday.
sceneCN: 这里 eightieth 是「第八十个」（第 1 个义项：排在另外七十九个之后的位置）；句意是全村人来给她过第八十个生日。

pos.zh: 数词（序数）：第八十；八十分之一
名词：第八十个；八十分之一；（口语）八十岁生日

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉序数词尾 -eth 并还原 y 得到，义为「八十」

senses.title: The eightieth in order
senses.definition: coming after seventy-nine others in a series
senses.definitionCN: 在一串中排在另外七十九个之后
senses.example: The eightieth page is missing from this copy.
senses.exampleCN: 这一本缺了第八十页。
senses.why: Eightieth is eighty plus the ordinal -eth, with y changed to ie; it marks the place after seventy-nine others.
senses.whyCN: eightieth 是 eighty 加序数词尾 -eth、y 变 ie 而成，标记的是排在七十九个之后的位置。

senses.title: One of eighty equal parts
senses.definition: one of eighty equal parts of a whole
senses.definitionCN: 一个整体被均分为八十份时的一份
senses.example: An eightieth of the profit goes to the fund.
senses.exampleCN: 利润的八十分之一进入基金。
senses.why: Cut a whole into eighty and each piece is an eightieth, the ordinal used as a fraction.
senses.whyCN: 把一个整体切成八十份，每一份就是一个 eightieth，序数词被当作分数使用。

senses.title: An eightieth birthday
senses.definition: the birthday on which someone turns eighty, or the celebration of it
senses.definitionCN: 某人满八十岁那天的生日，或为此举行的庆祝
senses.example: The whole village came to her eightieth birthday.
senses.exampleCN: 全村人都来给她过八十岁生日。
senses.why: Counting years in order reaches the eightieth, so the ordinal stands alone as the name of that birthday.
senses.whyCN: 按顺序数年份会数到第八十个，于是这个序数词单独成词，成了那个生日的名字。

intro.en: Eightieth is Old English eahtatiggoða, the ordinal of eahtatig, eighty, which was itself eight groups of ten.
intro.cn: eightieth 是古英语 eahtatiggoða，即 eahtatig（八十）的序数形式，而八十本身就是八个十。

items.en: Eahta meant eight and begins the whole family.
items.cn: eahta 意为「八」，是整个词族的起点。

items.en: The element tig meant a group of ten, so eahtatig was eight tens.
items.cn: 成分 tig 意为「一组十」，所以 eahtatig 就是八个十。

items.en: The compound named eighty, the count built on eight.
items.cn: 这个复合词指八十，是建立在「八」上的计数。

items.en: The ordinal added the -tha ending to mark the eightieth place.
items.cn: 序数形式加上 -tha 词尾，标记第八十的位置。

items.en: Middle English reshaped the ending to -ethe and later -ieth.
items.cn: 中古英语把词尾改写为 -ethe，后来又变成 -ieth。

items.en: The modern form is eighty plus -eth, with y written as ie.
items.cn: 现代词形是 eighty 加 -eth，其中 y 写作 ie。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the numerals built on eight; the near-meaning group gathers words for late old age and for a hundredth part.
note.cn: 形近组收由 eight 构成的数词；近义组收表示高龄与百分之一的词。

entries.definition: A special anniversary, often a fiftieth or a significant round number.

normalIntro.en: These hooks build the word from eight tens, then bend the tail into an ordinal and a fraction.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从八个十出发，再把词尾弯成序数词与分数。

normal.en: One eightieth is a very thin slice of a whole.
normal.cn: 八十分之一是从整体上切下的极薄一片。

normal.en: Candles crowd the cake: that is an eightieth birthday.
normal.cn: 蜡烛挤满蛋糕：那就是第八十个生日。

senses.title: The number eighty
senses.definition: the number 80, eight times ten
senses.definitionCN: 数字 80，即八乘十
senses.example: The old car's dial goes no higher than eighty.
senses.exampleCN: 那辆旧车的速度表最高只到八十。
senses.why: Eighty is the old compound eight-ten-group, a count that simply multiplies eight by a group of ten.
senses.whyCN: eighty 是「八组十」这个古老复合词，把八乘以一组十所得的那个计数。

senses.title: The years 1980 to 1989
senses.definition: the decade between 1980 and 1989, usually written the eighties
senses.definitionCN: 1980 到 1989 之间的十年，通常写作 the eighties
senses.example: The music of the eighties still fills the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 八十年代的音乐至今仍充满大厅。
senses.why: Years are counted by their tens, so each decade takes the plural numeral as its name.
senses.whyCN: 年份按十位来数，于是每个十年就用这个数词的复数作名称。

senses.title: The ages eighty to eighty-nine
senses.definition: the period of life between the ages of eighty and eighty-nine, usually in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 八十岁到八十九岁之间的人生阶段，通常用复数
senses.example: She took up painting in her eighties.
senses.exampleCN: 她在八十多岁时开始学画。
senses.why: A decade of years looks the same whether it is history or a life, so the eighties can also name an age band.
senses.whyCN: 十年的跨度无论是历史还是人生看起来都一样，所以 the eighties 也能指一个年龄段。

definition_zh: 两者中任一的；两者各一的；也（用于否定）；或者
definition_en: one or the other of two, each of the two, also in a negative sentence, or used in either or
core_image: 两条并排的路，站在岔口的人只能挑一条
scene: 路口只分出两条路，她把水壶检查了两遍才动身。Either road will take you to the mill.
sceneCN: 这里 either 是「两者中任一的」（第 1 个义项：两条路里的任何一条）；句意是两条路中哪一条都能到磨坊。

senses.title: One or the other of two
senses.definition: one or the other of two people or things, it does not matter which
senses.definitionCN: 两个人或物中的任何一个，不论哪一个
senses.example: Either road will take you to the mill.
senses.exampleCN: 两条路中哪一条都能到磨坊。
senses.why: Either began as the old word for each of two, and a free choice between two grew out of that.
senses.whyCN: either 最初是「两者各自」的古老说法，两者之间的自由选择就从这个意思长出来。

senses.title: Each of the two
senses.definition: each of the two, used after a singular noun to mean both sides
senses.definitionCN: 两者各自，用在单数名词后表示两边的意思
senses.example: The lane is lined with poplars on either side.
senses.exampleCN: 小路两边都种着白杨。
senses.why: The older sense of each survives in phrases like on either side, where both sides are meant.
senses.whyCN: 更古老的「各自」义保留在 on either side 这样的说法里，实际指的是两边。

senses.title: Also, in a negative sentence
senses.definition: used at the end of a negative statement to add another negative point
senses.definitionCN: 用于否定句末尾，再补充一个否定内容
senses.example: I have not finished, and my brother has not either.
senses.exampleCN: 我没做完，我弟弟也没做完。
senses.why: If not one of two is so, then not the other one either: the pronoun turns into a sentence-ending adverb.
senses.whyCN: 如果两者之一不是如此，那么另一个也不是：代词就这样变成了句末副词。

senses.title: Either or as a pair
senses.definition: used before two choices to show that one of them must be chosen
senses.definitionCN: 用在两个选项之前，表示必须从中选择一个
senses.example: Either you sign now or you lose the place.
senses.exampleCN: 你要么现在签字，要么就失去这个名额。
senses.why: The choice between two is stated as a pair, and either heads the first branch of the fork.
senses.whyCN: 两者之间的选择被摆成一对，either 站在岔路的第一条分支上。

intro.en: Either comes from Old English ǣgther, a contraction of ǣghwæther, each of two, from the root that also gives each.
intro.cn: either 来自古英语 ǣgther，是 ǣghwæther（两者各自）的缩合形式，其词根也生出 each。

items.en: The compound meant each of the two, built on a root meaning ever and which.
items.cn: 这个复合词意为「两者各自」，建立在表示「每一个、哪一个」的词根上。

items.en: The contracted form kept the sense of each of two without exception.
items.cn: 缩合形式保留「两者中无一例外」的意思。

items.en: Further contraction produced ǣgther, the direct ancestor of either.
items.cn: 进一步缩合产生 ǣgther，即 either 的直系祖先。

items.en: Middle English weakened the first sound and settled the spelling.
items.cn: 中古英语弱化了第一个音，固定了拼写。

items.en: The sense widened from each of two to one or the other, and the adverb use grew from negatives.
items.cn: 词义从「两者各自」扩展到「两者之一」，副词用法则从否定句中长出。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the paired determiners; the near-meaning group separates any, both and neither.
note.cn: 形近组收成对的限定词；近义组区分 any、both 与 neither。

entries.definition: Not one and not the other of two, the negative partner of either.

entries.definition: A substance once thought to fill all space, or a chemical solvent.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「以太」或「乙醚」，拼写相近但来源不同。

entries.definition: Very keen to do something.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「热切的」，与 either 仅部分拼写相似。

entries.definition: One or some of a larger set, not limited to two.
entries.definitionCN: 限定词，义为「任何」，范围大于两个。

entries.definition: The two together, not one of them.
entries.definitionCN: 限定词，义为「两者都」，是合起来而不是选一个。

entries.definition: Any one of a set that is not limited to two.
entries.definitionCN: 代词，义为「无论哪一个」，不限于两个。

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin at a fork with two roads, then show how the same word becomes both, also, and a paired choice.

normal.en: Either lives at a fork: exactly two roads, and you take one.
normal.cn: either 住在岔口：正好两条路，你走其中一条。

normal.en: On either side means on both sides, the older sense of each.
normal.cn: on either side 指两边，是「各自」这个更古老的意思。

normal.en: In a negative sentence, either moves to the end and means too.
normal.cn: 在否定句里，either 跑到句末，意思是「也」。

normal.en: Either you stay or you go: the fork is spoken as a pair.
normal.cn: 要么留、要么走：岔口被说成了一对。

normal.en: Add n and you get neither, the fork with no road taken.
normal.cn: 前面加 n 就成了 neither，即两条路都不走。

abstract.en: Picture a stone signpost with two arms pointing different ways.
abstract.cn: 想象一块石制路牌，两条手臂指向不同方向。

abstract.en: The same post can name one road, both roads, or a refusal of both.
abstract.cn: 同一块路牌可以说一条路、两条路，或两条都不走。

abstract.en: Either is a choice held open at the moment before it is made.
abstract.cn: either 就是选择做出之前那个仍然敞开的状态。

examples.en: Either road will take you to the mill.
examples.cn: 两条路中哪一条都能到磨坊。

examples.en: The lane is lined with poplars on either side.
examples.cn: 小路两边都种着白杨。

examples.en: I have not finished, and my brother has not either.
examples.cn: 我没做完，我弟弟也没做完。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「挨则」——岔口两条路，挨着挑哪条都行

root: 古英语 ǣgther 是 ǣghwæther「两者各自」的缩合形式，词根同时生出 each；词义由「各自」扩展为「两者之一」，再由否定句生出「也」。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses of either: one of two, each of the two, also in negatives, and the paired choice either or.
sensesIntro.cn: either 的四个义项：两者之一、两者各自、否定句中的「也」，以及 either or 的成对选择。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fork with exactly two roads and a traveller who must pick one.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个只有两条路的岔口，行人必须挑一条。

branches.en: THE CHOICE: one road, it does not matter which.
branches.cn: 选择线：走一条，不限哪条。

branches.en: THE PAIR: each of the two, as in on either side.
branches.cn: 成对线：两者各自，如 on either side。

branches.en: THE NEGATIVE: not one, and not the other either.
branches.cn: 否定线：一个不是，另一个也不是。

branches.en: THE FORK SPOKEN ALOUD: either this or that.
branches.cn: 出声的岔口：或者这个，或者那个。

branches.en: THE TWO ENDS: choosing one and naming both grow from the same pair.
branches.cn: 两端线：选一个与指两者，都从同一对里长出。

intro.en: Either is a worn-down Old English compound rather than a prefixed Latin word; its parts are no longer separable.
intro.cn: either 是磨蚀的古英语复合词，而非拉丁语加前缀的词；它的构件今天已不可再分。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic and has no Latin layer; the Indo-European root behind the old compound is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属于日耳曼语，没有拉丁语层次；古老复合词背后的印欧词根属于重构。

items.example: It is the full early form.
It is a shortened form of the compound.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个复合词的缩短形式。

items.example: It is the direct source form.

items.meaning: every one of two or more
items.example: It shares the same old root.
items.exampleCN: 它与本词共用同一个古老词根。

items.example: It is either with a negative first element.
items.exampleCN: 它是 either 前加否定成分。
它由 either 与 or 复合。

items.example: It survives inside the old pair words.
items.exampleCN: 它残留在这一对古词之中。
它标记这种二选一的对比。

definition_zh: 精心制作的；繁复的；详尽的；详细阐述
definition_en: having many carefully arranged parts, planned in great detail, or to explain something more fully
core_image: 一件木雕上刻满细密的缠枝纹，刀刀不省
scene: 那张桌子的每条腿都雕满缠枝纹，做的人不肯省一刀。The table has an elaborate carved base.
sceneCN: 这里 elaborate 是「繁复精细的」（第 1 个义项：部件众多且精心安排）；句意是这张桌子的底座雕工繁复。

pos.zh: 形容词：精心制作的；繁复的；详尽的
动词：详细阐述；进一步说明

forms.label: 比较级（形容词，多音节用 more）
最高级（形容词，多音节用 most）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「详述；精心制作」
由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「繁复地；精心地」
由 elaborate 加 -ness 构成，义为「繁复；精细」

senses.title: Having many carefully made parts
senses.definition: having many parts or details that were made with care, sometimes more than is needed
senses.definitionCN: 部件或细节众多且制作精心，有时多到超出必要
senses.example: The table has an elaborate carved base.
senses.exampleCN: 这张桌子的底座雕工繁复。
senses.why: Elaborate is Latin elaboratus, worked out; labour is visible in every added part.
senses.whyCN: elaborate 是拉丁语 elaboratus，意为「做出来的」；每多一个部件，都能看见那份劳作。

senses.title: Planned in great detail
senses.definition: worked out with great care and in many steps, as a plan or system
senses.definitionCN: 经过细致推敲、步骤繁多，如计划或体系
senses.example: They worked out an elaborate plan for the escape.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为逃跑制定了一套周密的计划。
senses.why: A plan is also a thing made, so the same word covers the labour of thought rather than of hands.
senses.whyCN: 计划同样是被做出来的东西，于是同一个词也能覆盖头脑的劳作而不只是手上的。

senses.title: To explain more fully
senses.definition: to add more detail to what has been said or written
senses.definitionCN: 为已说或已写的内容补充更多细节
senses.example: Could you elaborate on that last point?
senses.exampleCN: 你能就最后一点详细说明吗？
senses.why: To elaborate is to keep working the material until the shape is complete, so speech is treated like wood.
senses.whyCN: elaborate 就是继续加工材料直到形状完整，于是言语也被当成木头来雕。

intro.en: Elaborate comes from Latin elaboratus, the past participle of elaborare, to labour out, from e- out plus laborare, to work.
intro.cn: elaborate 来自拉丁语 elaboratus，即 elaborare（费力做出）的过去分词，由 e-（出）加 laborare（劳作）构成。

items.en: Labor meant toil or effort, the noun behind the verb.
items.cn: labor 意为「辛劳、费力」，是动词背后的名词。

items.en: The verb meant to work, to toil or to be in difficulty.
items.cn: 这个动词意为「劳作、辛苦、处于困难」。

items.en: E- out plus laborare formed the verb to work out or take pains over.
items.cn: e-（出）加 laborare 构成「做出来、为之费力」的动词。

items.en: The participle described something worked out with care, hence finely made.
items.cn: 分词描述经过仔细加工而成的东西，因此是「精细制作的」。

items.en: English borrowed the adjective for ornamented things and later formed a verb from it.
items.cn: 英语借入这个形容词指装饰繁复之物，后来又由它造出动词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the elaboration family; the near-meaning group separates intricate, detailed and ornate.
note.cn: 形近组收 elaboration 词族；近义组区分 intricate、detailed 与 ornate。

entries.definition: The act of explaining in more detail, or of working something out fully.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「详述；精心制作」，由 elaborate 加 -ion 构成。

entries.definition: In a detailed or heavily ornamented manner.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「繁复地；精心地」。

entries.definition: Work, especially hard physical work; the root of elaborate.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「劳动」，是本词的词根来源。

entries.definition: Having many small parts arranged in a way that is hard to follow.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「错综复杂的」，强调难以看清的结构。

entries.definition: Containing many facts or small points, without the sense of ornament.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「详细的」，只有细节多，不含装饰义。

entries.definition: Richly decorated; it stresses decoration rather than planning.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「华丽装饰的」，强调装饰而非谋划。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a carving knife, then move to a plan on paper and finally to a speaker adding detail.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从一把刻刀出发，再走到纸上的计划，最后落到补充细节的说话人。

normal.en: Elaborate carries labour in it: every extra part cost work.
normal.cn: elaborate 里藏着 labour：每多一个部件都是劳作。

normal.en: A carved table leg is elaborate; a plain one is not.
normal.cn: 雕花的桌腿是 elaborate，光的就不是。

normal.en: A plan can be as elaborate as a carving.
normal.cn: 一份计划可以和一件雕刻一样繁复。

normal.en: To elaborate on a point is to keep carving it.
normal.cn: elaborate on 一点，就是继续雕那一点。

normal.en: Elaborate is the adjective; elaborate is also the verb, same spelling.
normal.cn: elaborate 既是形容词也是动词，拼写相同。

abstract.en: Picture a woodcarver who refuses to leave a surface plain.
abstract.cn: 想象一位不肯让任何平面空着的木雕师。

abstract.en: The same patience can go into a table, a plan, or an answer.
abstract.cn: 同一份耐性可以用在桌子、计划或一个回答上。

abstract.en: Elaborate means the work has been worked again and again.
abstract.cn: elaborate 意味着这件东西被一遍遍加工过。

examples.en: The table has an elaborate carved base.
examples.cn: 这张桌子的底座雕工繁复。

examples.en: They worked out an elaborate plan for the escape.
examples.cn: 他们为逃跑制定了一套周密的计划。

examples.en: Could you elaborate on that last point?
examples.cn: 你能就最后一点详细说明吗？

dict_mnemonic.text: 「伊拉伯瑞特」——桌腿刻满缠枝纹，一刀也不肯省

root: 拉丁语 laborare「劳作」加前缀 e-「出」构成 elaborare「费力做出」，其过去分词 elaboratus 意为「精心做成的」，英语借入为形容词，后又用作动词「详述」。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of elaborate: richly made, carefully planned in detail, and the verb meaning to explain more fully.
sensesIntro.cn: elaborate 的三个义项：制作繁复、谋划周密，以及动词「详细阐述」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a carved table leg covered in dense vine patterns, no cut spared.
core.cn: 核心意象：雕满细密缠枝纹的桌腿，一刀也不省。

branches.en: THE CARVING: many parts, each one worked by hand.
branches.cn: 雕工线：部件众多，每一件都手工加工。

branches.en: THE PLAN: the same patience spent on thought instead of wood.
branches.cn: 计划线：同一份耐性用在思虑而非木头上。

branches.en: THE EXPLANATION: the speaker keeps working the point.
branches.cn: 说明线：说话人继续加工那一点。

branches.en: THE DETAIL: whether hands or head, the detail is deliberate.
branches.cn: 细节线：无论用手还是用脑，细节都是有意加的。

branches.en: THE UNFOLDING: a detailed plan and a detailed answer both open outward.
branches.cn: 展开线：周密的计划与详尽的回答都向外铺开。

intro.en: Elaborate is e- plus the Latin labour verb; English then adds -ion, -ly and -ness.
intro.cn: elaborate 是 e- 加拉丁语「劳作」动词；英语随后再加 -ion、-ly 与 -ness。

latinIntro.en: Latin labor, laborare and elaboratus are all recorded, so only the deeper Indo-European root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 labor、laborare 与 elaboratus 均有记录，只有更深的印欧词根属于重构。

items.exampleCN: 它与 laborare 构成 elaborare。

definition_zh: 有弹性的；可伸缩的；灵活的；橡皮筋
definition_en: able to stretch and return to its shape, able to change or be changed easily, or a rubber band
core_image: 一根橡皮筋被拉到两倍长，一松手又缩回原样
scene: 她把那根旧橡皮筋绕了两圈，纸卷始终没散。A thick elastic held the rolled papers together.
sceneCN: 这里 elastic 是「橡皮筋」（第 4 个义项：可拉伸回弹的环状橡胶制品）；句意是一根粗橡皮筋把卷好的纸捆住了。

pos.zh: 形容词：有弹性的；可伸缩的；灵活的
名词：橡皮筋；弹性织物

forms.label: 比较级（形容词，多音节用 more）
最高级（形容词，多音节用 most）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「弹性；灵活性」
由本词加副词后缀 -ally 构成，义为「有弹性地」
由本词加否定前缀 in- 构成，义为「无弹性的；僵硬的」
由本词加 -ated 构成，义为「装有松紧带的」

senses.title: Able to stretch and spring back
senses.definition: able to be stretched and then return to its original shape
senses.definitionCN: 能够被拉伸，随后又恢复原来的形状
senses.example: The fabric is elastic enough to fit any wrist.
senses.exampleCN: 这块布料弹性足够，什么手腕都套得上。
senses.why: Elastic was coined from a Greek word for beaten metal that springs back, so the idea is a shape that returns.
senses.whyCN: elastic 由希腊语中表示「被敲打后能回弹的金属」的词造出，核心就是「会恢复的形状」。

senses.title: Able to change easily
senses.definition: able to change, adapt or be stretched in meaning without breaking
senses.definitionCN: 能够改变、适应，或在含义上被拉宽而不致崩坏
senses.example: The timetable is elastic enough to absorb delays.
senses.exampleCN: 这份时间表灵活得足以吸收延误。
senses.why: A material that springs back suggests a rule that gives and returns, so the adjective moves from rubber to arrangements.
senses.whyCN: 能回弹的材料让人想到一条会让步又收回的规则，于是这个形容词从橡皮走到了安排上。

senses.title: Responsive to price or demand
senses.definition: in economics, changing noticeably when price or income changes
senses.definitionCN: 在经济学中，随价格或收入变化而明显变化
senses.example: Demand for flights is highly elastic in summer.
senses.exampleCN: 夏季的机票需求弹性很大。
senses.why: A quantity that stretches with price behaves like rubber, so economists borrowed the same image.
senses.whyCN: 随价格伸缩的数量表现得像橡皮，于是经济学家借用了同一个意象。

senses.title: A rubber band
senses.definition: a loop of stretchy rubber used to hold things together
senses.definitionCN: 用来把东西捆在一起的环状弹性橡胶
senses.example: A thick elastic held the rolled papers together.
senses.exampleCN: 一根粗橡皮筋把卷好的纸捆住了。
senses.why: The adjective became a noun for the thing made of the material, the way a name for a quality becomes an object.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转成了用这种材料做成之物的名词，就像一种性质的名称变成了实物。

intro.en: Elastic was coined in the seventeenth century from Greek elastos, beaten or ductile, and Latin elasticus, in the new science of materials.
intro.cn: elastic 是十七世纪在材料新科学中造出的词，源自希腊语 elastos（可敲打延展的）与拉丁语 elasticus。

items.en: The verb meant to drive or set in motion, and it lies behind the later adjective.
items.cn: 这个动词意为「驱动、推动」，是后来形容词的深层来源。

items.en: Elastos described metal that could be beaten out and would spring back.
items.cn: elastos 描述可被敲打成薄片又会回弹的金属。

items.en: Modern Latin formed elasticus as a technical adjective for materials.
items.cn: 近代拉丁语构成 elasticus，作为材料的专业形容词。

items.en: Seventeenth-century writers used elastic for gases and springs that recover their shape.
items.cn: 十七世纪的作者用 elastic 指能恢复形状的气体与弹簧。

items.en: The word spread to cloth, timetables, prices and finally to the rubber band itself.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到布料、时间表、价格，最后连橡皮筋本身也叫 elastic。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the elasticity family; the near-meaning group separates flexible, springy and plastic.
note.cn: 形近组收 elasticity 词族；近义组区分 flexible、springy 与 plastic。

entries.definition: The ability to stretch and return, or the responsiveness of demand.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「弹性；灵活性」，由 elastic 加 -ity 构成。

entries.definition: Not able to stretch, or not responsive to price.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无弹性的」，由 in- 加 elastic 构成。

entries.definition: Bands or strips of stretchy material, used in the plural.
entries.definitionCN: 名词复数，指一根根弹性带。

entries.definition: Able to bend without breaking; it stresses bending rather than springing back.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可弯曲的」，强调弯而不断，而非回弹。

entries.definition: Bouncing back quickly, like a spring; more concrete and physical.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有弹力的」，像弹簧一样回跳，更具体。

entries.definition: Easily shaped when soft; it stresses moulding, not recovery.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可塑的」，强调塑形而不是恢复。

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with one rubber band, then let the same springiness travel into plans and prices.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从一根橡皮筋出发，再让同样的回弹力走进计划与价格。

normal.en: Stretch it, let go, and it returns: that is elastic.
normal.cn: 拉长、松手、回到原样：这就是 elastic。

normal.en: An elastic timetable gives way and then closes again.
normal.cn: 有弹性的时间表会让步，然后又收回去。

normal.en: Economists call demand elastic when buyers stretch away from a price rise.
normal.cn: 价格上涨时买家就缩手，经济学家称这种需求为 elastic。

normal.en: The band itself takes the name: a bag of elastics.
normal.cn: 橡皮筋本身也用了这个名字：一袋 elastics。

normal.en: In- turns it stiff: inelastic.
normal.cn: 加 in- 就变硬：inelastic。

abstract.en: Picture a rubber band pulled to twice its length.
abstract.cn: 想象一根橡皮筋被拉到两倍长。

abstract.en: The same give-and-return can describe a rule, a price or a schedule.
abstract.cn: 同一种「让开又回来」可以形容规则、价格或日程。

abstract.en: Elastic is any shape that remembers where it started.
abstract.cn: elastic 就是任何记得自己原位的形状。

examples.en: The fabric is elastic enough to fit any wrist.
examples.cn: 这块布料弹性足够，什么手腕都套得上。

examples.en: The timetable is elastic enough to absorb delays.
examples.cn: 这份时间表灵活得足以吸收延误。

examples.en: A thick elastic held the rolled papers together.
examples.cn: 一根粗橡皮筋把卷好的纸捆住了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「伊拉斯提克」——橡皮筋拉到两倍长，一松手缩回去

root: 源自希腊语 elastos「可敲打延展、会回弹的」，经近代拉丁语 elasticus 进入十七世纪科学英语，核心是「拉伸后恢复原形」。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses of elastic: springing back, bending to fit, responding to price, and the rubber band itself.
sensesIntro.cn: elastic 的四个义项：能回弹、能变通、随价格伸缩，以及橡皮筋本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rubber band stretched to twice its length and released.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根橡皮筋被拉到两倍长，然后松开。

branches.en: THE SPRING: the material returns to its old shape.
branches.cn: 回弹线：材料回到原来的形状。

branches.en: THE ROOM TO BEND: a plan or rule stretches and still holds.
branches.cn: 余量线：计划或规则被拉宽而依然成立。

branches.en: THE MARKET: buyers stretch away when prices rise.
branches.cn: 市场线：价格一涨，买家就缩手。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: the adjective becomes the name of the band.
branches.cn: 实物线：形容词变成了橡皮筋的名称。

branches.en: ONE IMAGE: physical springiness read into human arrangements.
branches.cn: 同一意象：把物理回弹读进人的安排里。

intro.en: Elastic is a scientific coinage from Greek and Latin; English adds -ity, -ally and the negative prefix in-.
intro.cn: elastic 是由希腊语与拉丁语造出的科学词汇；英语再加 -ity、-ally 与否定前缀 in-。

latinIntro.en: Greek elastos and Latin elasticus are recorded forms; the older Greek verb behind them is attested too.

definition_en: the joint between the upper arm and the forearm, the part of a sleeve covering it, or to push with the elbow
core_image: 手臂弯成一个直角，关节处顶出一块尖骨
scene: 人群一挤，他抬起手臂护住怀里的箱子，关节撞到了门框。He raised his elbow to shield the box.
sceneCN: 这里 elbow 是「肘」（第 1 个义项：上臂与前臂之间的关节）；句意是他抬起肘护住箱子。

pos.zh: 名词：肘；肘部；（管道）弯头
动词：用肘推；挤进

senses.title: The joint of the arm
senses.definition: the joint where the upper arm meets the forearm, and the bony point outside it
senses.definitionCN: 上臂与前臂相接的关节，以及外侧那块突出的骨头
senses.example: He raised his elbow to shield the box.
senses.exampleCN: 他抬起肘护住箱子。
senses.why: Old English elnboga joined the word for forearm length with the word for bow, so the joint is literally an arm-bow.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 elnboga 把「前臂长度」与「弓」两个词拼在一起，这个关节字面就是「手臂之弓」。

senses.title: The part of a sleeve
senses.definition: the part of a garment that covers the elbow, often reinforced
senses.definitionCN: 衣服覆盖肘部的那一块，常做加固
senses.example: The jacket has leather patches on the elbows.
senses.exampleCN: 这件外套的肘部有皮革补片。
senses.why: Clothing is named after the body part it covers, so the sleeve's bend is also an elbow.
senses.whyCN: 衣服的部件按它覆盖的身体部位命名，于是袖子的弯处也叫 elbow。

senses.title: To push with the elbow
senses.definition: to push someone or make a way through a crowd using the elbows
senses.definitionCN: 用肘推开别人或在人群中挤出一条路
senses.example: She elbowed her way to the front of the queue.
senses.exampleCN: 她用肘挤到了队伍前面。
senses.why: The hard point of the joint becomes a tool, and the noun turns into the action of using it.
senses.whyCN: 关节上那块硬骨变成工具，名词也就转成「用它去推」的动作。

senses.title: A bend in a pipe
senses.definition: a sharp bend in a pipe or chimney, or the fitting that makes it
senses.definitionCN: 管道或烟道中的急弯，或做成这个弯的管件
senses.example: A blocked elbow stopped the water flow.
senses.exampleCN: 一个堵塞的弯头阻断了水流。
senses.why: A pipe that turns at an angle imitates the bent arm, so plumbers borrowed the body word.
senses.whyCN: 管道拐出一个角度就像弯起的手臂，于是管道工借用了这个身体词。

intro.en: Elbow comes from Old English elnboga, a compound of eln, forearm, and boga, bow, the same bow of bow and arrow.
intro.cn: elbow 来自古英语 elnboga，由 eln（前臂）与 boga（弓）复合，boga 就是弓箭之「弓」。

items.en: The reconstructed noun named the forearm and also a unit of length.
items.cn: 重构名词既指前臂，也指一种长度单位。

items.en: Eln meant the forearm and the old measure called the ell.
items.cn: eln 指前臂，也指称为「厄尔」的旧长度单位。

items.en: Boga meant bow, the curved weapon and any arch.
items.cn: boga 意为「弓」，既是弯的武器，也指任何拱形。

items.en: The compound named the arm's bend, the elbow.
items.cn: 这个复合词指手臂弯处，即肘。

items.en: Middle English smoothed the middle of the word and settled elbowe.
items.cn: 中古英语磨平了词的中段，固定为 elbowe。

items.en: The verb use and the pipe sense grew from the shape and the joint.
items.cn: 动词用法与管道义分别从「形状」与「关节」长出来。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers compounds built on elbow; the near-meaning group separates joint, wrist, knee and shoulder.
note.cn: 形近组收由 elbow 构成的复合词；近义组区分关节与相邻部位。

entries.definition: An old unit of length based on the forearm, from the same eln.

entries.definition: Any place where two bones meet; the general word for what elbow names in particular.

entries.definition: The joint at the top of the arm, above the elbow.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「肩」，位于肘之上的关节。

definition_en: rather old, used politely of people past middle age, or the group of old people as a whole
core_image: 公园长椅上，一位老人把围巾又拢紧了些
scene: 长椅上那位老人扶着扶手才站起来，动作很慢。An elderly man rose slowly from the bench.
sceneCN: 这里 elderly 是「年长的」（第 1 个义项：客气地指已过中年、年纪较大的人）；句意是一位年长的男士慢慢从长椅上站起来。

pos.zh: 形容词：年长的；上了年纪的（较礼貌）
名词：the elderly 老年人（集合）

senses.title: Rather old, said politely
senses.definition: past middle age and getting old, used as a polite word instead of old
senses.definitionCN: 已过中年、渐渐年老，用作 old 的客气说法
senses.example: An elderly man rose slowly from the bench.
senses.exampleCN: 一位年长的男士慢慢从长椅上站起来。
senses.why: Elderly is elder plus -ly, and elder is the comparative of old: it says older, gently, without the bluntness of old.
senses.whyCN: elderly 是 elder 加 -ly，而 elder 是 old 的比较级：它温和地说「更年长」，没有 old 那么直白。

senses.title: Old people as a group
senses.definition: with the, old people considered as a group in society
senses.definitionCN: 与 the 连用，指社会中作为一个群体的老年人
senses.example: The clinic offers free transport for the elderly.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所为老年人提供免费接送。
senses.why: An adjective with the can name a whole class, so the elderly means all who answer to that description.
senses.whyCN: 形容词加 the 可以指整个类别，所以 the elderly 就是所有符合这个描述的人。

senses.title: Old and worn, said with a smile
senses.definition: used humorously of things that are old and worn out
senses.definitionCN: 戏谑地用于年久失修、老旧的物件
senses.example: My elderly laptop takes ten minutes to start.
senses.exampleCN: 我那台老掉牙的笔记本要十分钟才启动。
senses.why: The polite word for old people is transferred to machines, and the politeness itself becomes the joke.
senses.whyCN: 这个对人客气的词被挪到机器上，那份客气本身就成了笑话。

intro.en: Elderly is elder plus -ly; elder is the old comparative of old, from Old English eldra, and still carries the sense of seniority.
intro.cn: elderly 是 elder 加 -ly；elder 是 old 的古老比较级，来自古英语 eldra，至今仍带「辈分较长」的意味。

items.en: The reconstructed adjective meant old or grown up.
items.cn: 重构形容词意为「年老的、长成的」。

items.en: Eldra was the comparative of eald, old, and meant older.
items.cn: eldra 是 eald（老）的比较级，意为「更年长的」。

items.en: Elder kept the sense of senior in age or rank, especially within a family.
items.cn: elder 保留年龄或辈分较长的意思，尤用于家族内部。

items.en: The ending -ly softened the adjective into a polite description of age.
items.cn: 词尾 -ly 把这个形容词软化，成为对年龄的客气描述。

items.en: The elderly settled as a collective name, and the word spread jokingly to worn objects.
items.cn: the elderly 固定为集合称谓，这个词又戏谑地扩展到破旧物件上。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the elder family; the near-meaning group separates old, senior and aged by tone.
note.cn: 形近组收 elder 词族；近义组按语气区分 old、senior 与 aged。

entries.definition: Older, especially of a relative or a person of authority in a community.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词兼名词，义为「年长的；长辈」，是本词的词基。

entries.definition: The oldest of a group, usually of brothers or sisters.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「最年长的」，多指兄弟姐妹中的老大。

entries.definition: Having lived a long time; plainer and blunter than elderly.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「老的」，比 elderly 更直白。

entries.definition: Older or higher in rank, often used in official contexts such as senior citizens.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「年长的、资深的」，常用于 senior citizens 等正式说法。

entries.definition: Very old; it can sound more formal or more pointed than elderly.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「年迈的」，比 elderly 更正式或更强调。

entries.definition: Growing old, said of a process rather than a person's state.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「老龄化的」，描述过程而非人的状态。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from elder as the gentle comparative of old, then follow the word into a group name and a joke about machines.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从 elder 这个温和的比较级出发，再走到群体称谓与关于机器的玩笑。

normal.en: Elderly is elder plus -ly: the polite way of saying older.
normal.cn: elderly 是 elder 加 -ly：说「更年长」时的客气说法。

normal.en: Old can sting; elderly steps back and leaves room.
normal.cn: old 可能刺人；elderly 往后退半步，留出余地。

normal.en: The elderly are not one person but a whole group.
normal.cn: the elderly 不是一个人，而是一整群人。

normal.en: My elderly laptop is a joke: the politeness is the point.
normal.cn: my elderly laptop 是个玩笑：那份客气本身就是笑点。

normal.en: Elderly usually starts around retirement age, old goes further.
normal.cn: elderly 大约从退休年龄起算，old 还要再往后。

abstract.en: Picture a slow rise from a park bench, hands on the armrest.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人双手扶着扶手，从公园长椅上慢慢起身。

abstract.en: The same politeness can cover a person, a group, or a tired machine.
abstract.cn: 同一份客气可以覆盖一个人、一群人，或一台疲惫的机器。

abstract.en: Elderly is old with a hand held out.
abstract.cn: elderly 就是伸出手扶一把的 old。

examples.cn: 一位年长的男士慢慢从长椅上站起来。

examples.en: The clinic offers free transport for the elderly.
examples.cn: 这家诊所为老年人提供免费接送。

examples.en: My elderly laptop takes ten minutes to start.
examples.cn: 我那台老掉牙的笔记本要十分钟才启动。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of elderly: politely old, old people as a group, and humorously worn out.
sensesIntro.cn: elderly 的三个义项：客气地说年长、作为群体的老年人，以及戏称物件老旧。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old person rising slowly from a bench, one hand on the armrest.
core.cn: 核心意象：一位老人扶着扶手，从长椅上慢慢起身。

branches.en: THE PERSON: past middle age, described politely.
branches.cn: 人物线：已过中年，用客气的方式描述。

branches.en: THE CLASS: with the, all such people together.
branches.cn: 群体线：加 the 指所有这样的人。

branches.en: THE JOKE: the same politeness spent on a tired laptop.

branches.en: THE TONE: the word's gentleness is what joins person and group.

branches.cn: 转移线：对年岁的敬重变成对物件年岁的假敬重。

definition_zh: 选举；推选；选择决定；当选而尚未就职的
definition_en: to choose someone by voting, to decide to do something, or describing someone chosen but not yet in office
core_image: 一只只手举起，票箱被封上，名字被念出来
scene: 会场里一只手接一只手举起，票数很快过半。The members elected a new chair by a clear majority.
sceneCN: 这里 elect 是「选举」（第 1 个义项：通过投票选出某人）；句意是成员以明显多数选出了新主席。

pos.zh: 动词：选举；推选；选择做（某事）
形容词：当选而尚未就职的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「选举」
由本词加 -ive 构成，义为「选举的；选修的；选修课」
由本词加 -or 构成，义为「选民；选举人」
由 elector 加 -al 构成，义为「选举的」

senses.title: To choose by voting
senses.definition: to choose a person for an office or position by voting
senses.definitionCN: 通过投票为某个职位选出某人
senses.example: The members elected a new chair by a clear majority.
senses.exampleCN: 成员以明显多数选出了新主席。
senses.why: Elect is Latin eligere, e- out plus legere to pick: the choice is picked out and then made public.
senses.whyCN: elect 是拉丁语 eligere，由 e-（出）加 legere（挑选）构成：这个选择被挑出来，然后公开。

senses.title: To decide to do something
senses.definition: to choose to do something, especially in formal or official language
senses.definitionCN: 选择去做某事，尤用于正式或官方语境
senses.example: The company elected to remain silent.
senses.exampleCN: 公司选择保持沉默。
senses.why: The same picking happens inside one head instead of a hall, so elect can mean simply to choose.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「挑选」发生在一个脑袋里而不是大厅里，所以 elect 也能只表示「选择」。

senses.title: Chosen but not yet in office
senses.definition: used after a title for someone who has been elected but has not yet taken up the post
senses.definitionCN: 用在头衔之后，指已经当选但尚未上任的人
senses.example: The president elect will be sworn in in January.
senses.exampleCN: 当选总统将于一月宣誓就职。
senses.why: The pick has been made but the office is still empty, so the adjective marks that gap in time.
senses.whyCN: 人选已经挑定，而职位还空着，于是这个形容词标记出这段时间空隙。

intro.en: Elect comes from Latin eligere, to pick out, from e- out plus legere, to choose or read, and reached English through the participle electus.
intro.cn: elect 来自拉丁语 eligere（挑出），由 e-（出）加 legere（挑选、读）构成，经分词 electus 进入英语。

items.en: Legere meant to gather, pick or read, and it also gave lecture and legend.
items.cn: legere 意为「收集、挑选、读」，也生出 lecture 与 legend。

items.en: E- out plus legere formed eligere, to pick out from among others.
items.cn: e-（出）加 legere 构成 eligere，意为「从众人中挑出来」。

items.en: The participle electus meant picked out, hence chosen.
items.cn: 分词 electus 意为「被挑出的」，因此是「被选中的」。

items.en: The noun named the act of picking out, the source of election.
items.cn: 名词指「挑选」这一动作，是 election 的来源。

items.en: English borrowed the verb for choosing a person to an office.
items.cn: 英语借入这个动词，指为某个职位选出人选。

items.en: The bare verb also took the milder sense of deciding, and the adjective use followed.
items.cn: 光杆动词又带上「决定」的温和义，形容词用法随后出现。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the election family; the near-meaning group separates choose, vote and appoint.
note.cn: 形近组收 election 词族；近义组区分 choose、vote 与 appoint。

entries.definition: The process of choosing someone by voting.

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a hall of raised hands, then narrow to one private decision and one gap before taking office.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从举手的大厅出发，再缩到一个人的私下决定，以及上任前的那段空缺。

normal.en: Elect is e- out plus legere pick: to pick someone out.
normal.cn: elect 是 e-（出）加 legere（挑）：把某人挑出来。

normal.en: A hall of raised hands makes a vote into an election.
normal.cn: 一片举起的手把投票变成一场选举。

normal.en: A board can elect to stay silent: no votes, just a choice.
normal.cn: 董事会可以 elect to 保持沉默：没有投票，只有选择。

normal.en: President elect means chosen but not yet sworn in.
normal.cn: president elect 指已经选出、尚未宣誓就职。

normal.en: The same root gives lecture: picking words out of a page.
normal.cn: 同一个词根也生出 lecture：从书页上把词挑出来读。

abstract.en: Picture a hand raised in a room full of hands.
abstract.cn: 想象满屋子的手，其中一只举了起来。

abstract.en: The same picking can be public or private, and it can leave a name standing alone.
abstract.cn: 同一种挑选可以是公开的或私下的，也可以让一个名字单独立着。

abstract.en: Elect means someone was taken out of the many on purpose.
abstract.cn: elect 意味着有人被有意地从众多中拿了出来。

examples.en: The members elected a new chair by a clear majority.
examples.cn: 成员以明显多数选出了新主席。

examples.en: The company elected to remain silent.
examples.cn: 公司选择保持沉默。

examples.en: The president elect will be sworn in in January.
examples.cn: 当选总统将于一月宣誓就职。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of elect: choosing by vote, deciding to do something, and the adjective for someone chosen but not yet in office.

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a forest of raised hands and one name read out of the box.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片举起的手，一个名字从票箱里被念出。

branches.en: THE VOTE: the many choose one for an office.
branches.cn: 投票线：众人为职位选出一人。

branches.en: THE DECISION: the picking happens inside one mind.
branches.cn: 决定线：挑选发生在一个人心里。

branches.en: THE GAP: chosen already, in office not yet.
branches.cn: 空档线：已经选出，尚未上任。

branches.cn: 同一动作：公开投票与私下选择都是同一种挑出。

branches.cn: 等待线：投票结束，头衔还在等。

senses.title: The process of voting someone in
senses.definition: the organized process in which people vote to choose someone for an office
senses.definitionCN: 人们投票为某个职位选出人选的整套组织过程
senses.example: The election result came before midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 选举结果在午夜前出来了。
senses.why: Election is the noun of eligere, to pick out: the whole machinery exists for one act of picking.
senses.whyCN: election 是 eligere（挑出）的名词：整套机器只为一次「挑出」而存在。

senses.title: The fact of being chosen
senses.definition: the state or event of being chosen for a post, seen from the winner's side
senses.definitionCN: 从当选者角度看，被选上某个职位这一事实
senses.example: Her election to the board surprised no one.
senses.exampleCN: 她当选董事，没人感到意外。
senses.why: The same picking seen from inside the winner becomes a personal event rather than a public process.
senses.whyCN: 同一次挑选若从当选者内部看，就成了个人事件，而不是公共过程。

senses.title: A formal act of choosing
senses.definition: a deliberate choice between options, used in formal or religious language
senses.definitionCN: 在选项之间作出的慎重选择，用于正式或宗教语境
senses.example: He made a deliberate election to stay silent.
senses.exampleCN: 他有意选择了保持沉默。
senses.why: Before it meant voting, the word simply named a choice; that older sense survives in formal prose.
senses.whyCN: 在表示「投票」之前，这个词只指一次选择；这个更古老的意思仍活在正式文章里。

intro.en: Election comes from Latin electio, the noun of eligere, to pick out, formed from e- out and legere, to choose.
intro.cn: election 来自拉丁语 electio，即 eligere（挑出）的名词，由 e-（出）与 legere（挑选）构成。

items.en: Legere meant to gather or pick, and it also gave lecture and legend.
items.cn: legere 意为「收集、挑选」，也生出 lecture 与 legend。

items.en: E- out plus legere formed the verb to pick out from among others.
items.cn: e-（出）加 legere 构成「从众人中挑出」的动词。

items.en: Electio named the act of picking out, at first any choice at all.
items.cn: electio 指「挑出」的动作，最初泛指任何选择。

items.en: French narrowed the noun toward choosing a person for an office.
items.cn: 法语把这个名词窄化为「为职位选人」。

items.en: English used it for both the choice and the gathering that makes it.
items.cn: 英语既用它指选择本身，也指做出选择的那场集会。

items.en: The voting sense dominates, while the plain sense of choice survives in formal style.
items.cn: 投票义占了主导，而朴素的「选择」义仍留在正式文体中。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the elect family; the near-meaning group separates vote, ballot and referendum.
note.cn: 形近组收 elect 词族；近义组区分 vote、ballot 与 referendum。

entries.definition: The paper or system used to cast a vote, or the voting itself.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「选票、无记名投票」，指投票用的纸或方式。

entries.definition: A direct vote by the public on a single question, not on a person.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「公投」，就一个问题而非人选直接投票。

normal.en: A general election fills many seats on one day.

abstract.en: Election is a crowd doing the work of one hand.

senses.title: Filled by election
senses.definition: of a post or body, filled or decided by voting rather than by appointment
senses.definitionCN: 指职位或机构，由投票产生而非任命
senses.example: The mayor holds an elective office.
senses.exampleCN: 市长这一职位是民选的。
senses.why: Elective is elect plus -ive: the post has the property of being filled by a picking out.
senses.whyCN: elective 是 elect 加 -ive：这个职位带有「靠挑出来填补」的性质。

senses.title: Chosen rather than required
senses.definition: of a course or subject, taken by choice and not required
senses.definitionCN: 指课程或科目，出于自愿而非必修
senses.example: Music is an elective subject at this school.
senses.exampleCN: 在这所学校，音乐是选修科目。
senses.why: A student picking a course repeats the same picking out, so the word moves from offices to classrooms.
senses.whyCN: 学生挑一门课重复的是同一种「挑出」，于是这个词从职位走到了教室。

senses.title: Having the right to vote
senses.definition: of a person or body, possessing the right to vote in elections
senses.definitionCN: 指人或机构，拥有在选举中投票的权利
senses.example: The upper house is partly elective and partly appointed.
senses.exampleCN: 上议院部分由选举产生，部分由任命产生。
senses.why: The right to do the picking is itself described by the same adjective, so elective also means entitled to vote.
senses.whyCN: 做这次「挑出」的权利也用同一个形容词描述，所以 elective 也指「有选举权」。

senses.title: A course freely chosen
senses.definition: a course that a student chooses to take rather than one required by the programme
senses.definitionCN: 学生自愿选择而非培养方案规定的课程
senses.example: Students may take one elective in their final year.
senses.exampleCN: 学生在最后一年可以修一门选修课。
senses.why: The adjective becomes a noun for the thing chosen, the way a quality becomes an object.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转成「被选中之物」的名词，就像一种性质变成了实物。

senses.title: Scheduled rather than urgent
senses.definition: of medical treatment, planned in advance rather than needed at once
senses.definitionCN: 指医疗处置，事先安排而非当下必须进行
senses.example: The operation was elective, so it could wait a month.
senses.exampleCN: 这台手术是择期的，所以可以等一个月。
senses.why: What can be chosen in time is what is not forced by emergency, so elective also marks the optional in medicine.
senses.whyCN: 能在时间上挑选的，就是不被急症逼迫的，所以 elective 在医学里也标出「可选择」的部分。

intro.en: Elective is Latin electivus, from eligere, to pick out, with the adjective ending -ivus; English uses it for posts, courses and treatments.
intro.cn: elective 是拉丁语 electivus，由 eligere（挑出）加形容词词尾 -ivus 构成；英语把它用于职位、课程与医疗。

items.en: Legere meant to pick or gather, the base of the family.
items.cn: legere 意为「挑选、收集」，是整个词族的词基。

items.en: E- out plus legere formed the verb to pick out.
items.cn: e-（出）加 legere 构成「挑出」的动词。

items.en: The adjective described something that operates by choice or election.
items.cn: 这个形容词描述靠选择或选举来运作的事物。

items.en: Church and university Latin applied it to offices that were filled by voting.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语把它用于靠投票填补的职位。

items.en: English added the school sense of a chosen course and the medical sense of planned treatment.
items.cn: 英语又加入「自选课程」与「择期治疗」两个义项。

normal.cn: elective 是 elect 加 -ive：靠挑选来填补或取得的东西。

abstract.en: Elective marks whatever is left open to choice.

senses.title: Of electricity itself
senses.definition: relating to electricity as a physical force, as in current, charge or field
senses.definitionCN: 指作为物理力量的电，如电流、电荷、电场
senses.example: The electric charge built up on the dry cloth.
senses.exampleCN: 干燥的布上积聚起了电荷。
senses.why: Electric comes from amber, which when rubbed attracts things; the word first named that force itself.
senses.whyCN: electric 来自琥珀，摩擦后会吸东西；这个词最初指的就是那股力量本身。

senses.title: Working by electricity
senses.definition: of a machine or device, driven by electricity rather than by fuel or by hand
senses.definitionCN: 指机器或设备，由电力而非燃料或人力驱动
senses.example: The electric kettle switched itself off with a click.
senses.exampleCN: 那只电水壶咔一声自动断电。
senses.why: Once the force had a name, anything running on it was simply described with the same adjective.
senses.whyCN: 这股力量一旦有了名字，任何靠它运转的东西就用同一个形容词来描述。

senses.title: Tense with excitement
senses.definition: filled with a tense, exciting feeling, as if a current were running through it
senses.definitionCN: 充满紧张兴奋的感觉，仿佛有电流穿过
senses.example: The hall went electric when the band walked on.
senses.exampleCN: 乐队一上台，整个大厅就沸腾了。
senses.why: A shock runs through the body, so a crowd in suspense is described as carrying the same current.
senses.whyCN: 电击会穿过身体，于是屏息的人群也被说成带着同一股电流。

intro.en: Electric was coined in the seventeenth century from Latin electrum, amber, from Greek elektron, because rubbed amber attracts light objects.
intro.cn: electric 是十七世纪由拉丁语 electrum（琥珀）造出，源自希腊语 elektron，因为摩擦过的琥珀会吸起轻物。

items.en: Elektron meant amber, the fossil resin that first showed the effect.
items.cn: elektron 意为「琥珀」，就是最先显现这种效应的树脂化石。

items.en: Latin kept electrum for amber and for a pale gold alloy.
items.cn: 拉丁语用 electrum 指琥珀，也指一种淡金色的合金。

items.en: Seventeenth-century scientists formed electricus for the force shown by rubbed amber.
items.cn: 十七世纪科学家造出 electricus，指摩擦琥珀所显现的那股力。

items.en: English borrowed the adjective and applied it first to bodies that attract.
items.cn: 英语借入这个形容词，最初用于会吸引轻物的物体。

items.en: Industry widened it to machines, and writers stretched it to excitement.
items.cn: 工业把它扩展到机器，作家又把它拉向情绪上的激动。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the electricity family; the near-meaning group separates electrical, electronic and electrifying.
note.cn: 形近组收 electricity 词族；近义组区分 electrical、electronic 与 electrifying。

entries.definition: Relating to electricity as a system or field of engineering, rather than to one device.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「与电有关的、电气的」，指系统或工程，而非单个器具。

entries.definition: The energy carried by moving charges, or the supply of it.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「电；电力」。

entries.definition: A person who installs and repairs electrical wiring.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「电工」。

entries.definition: To charge with electricity, or to thrill suddenly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使带电；使震惊」。

entries.definition: Working by controlling tiny charged particles in circuits, as computers do.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「电子的」，靠控制电路中的带电微粒工作。

entries.definition: Extremely exciting; the feeling sense pushed to its strongest.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「极其震撼的」，把情绪义推到最强。

entries.definition: Driven by a stated source, as in battery-powered.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「以……为动力的」，需说明动力来源。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with amber and a spark, then run the same current through kettles and through a crowd.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从琥珀与火花出发，再让同一股电流通过水壶与人群。

normal.en: Electric comes from amber: rub it and it pulls threads toward it.
normal.cn: electric 来自琥珀：摩擦之后它会把细线吸过来。

normal.en: Electric names the force; electrical names the system built around it.
normal.cn: electric 指那股力本身；electrical 指围绕它建立的系统。

normal.en: An electric kettle has a plug; an electrical fault has a cause.
normal.cn: electric kettle 有插头；electrical fault 有原因。

normal.en: A hall can go electric without a single wire.
normal.cn: 大厅可以一根电线也没有却「带电」。

normal.en: Electronic is one step further: not just current, but circuits controlling it.
normal.cn: electronic 再进一步：不只是电流，而是控制电流的电路。

abstract.en: Picture a fingertip an inch from a door handle, a spark about to jump.
abstract.cn: 想象指尖离门把手一寸，火花就要跳过去。

abstract.en: The same jump can power a kettle or run through a waiting audience.
abstract.cn: 同一次跳跃可以带动水壶，也可以穿过等待的观众。

abstract.en: Electric is energy looking for somewhere to go.
abstract.cn: electric 就是一股急着找去处的能力。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of electric: the physical force itself, devices driven by it, and a mood charged like a current.
sensesIntro.cn: electric 的三个义项：电这股物理力量本身、靠它驱动的器具，以及像电流一样紧绷的情绪。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spark jumping from a fingertip to a door handle.
core.cn: 核心意象：一簇火花从指尖跳到门把手上。

branches.en: THE FORCE: current, charge and field as physics names them.
branches.cn: 力量线：物理学所说的电流、电荷与电场。

branches.en: THE DEVICE: a kettle or car that runs on that force.
branches.cn: 器具线：靠这股力运转的水壶或汽车。

branches.en: THE MOOD: a crowd charged like a wire.
branches.cn: 情绪线：人群像导线一样带电。

branches.en: THE SUPPLY: the force and the things it drives are one circuit.
branches.cn: 供给线：力量与它驱动的东西是同一条回路。

branches.en: THE SWITCH: a device turns on, and so does a room.
branches.cn: 开关线：器具被打开，房间也被打开。

intro.en: Electric is a scientific coinage on Greek amber; English adds -ity, -al, -ian, -fy and -onic.

senses.title: Relating to electrical systems
senses.definition: relating to electricity as a system of supply, wiring and engineering
senses.definitionCN: 指作为供电、布线与工程系统的电
senses.example: She studied electrical engineering at college.
senses.exampleCN: 她在大学学的是电气工程。
senses.why: The -al ending turns the noun electricity into a word about the field as a whole, so it suits systems rather than single devices.
senses.whyCN: -al 词尾把名词 electricity 变成指整个领域的词，因此它适合系统而不适合单个器具。

senses.title: Running on electricity
senses.definition: of equipment or appliances, operated by electricity, used as a general classifying word
senses.definitionCN: 指设备或器具由电力驱动，用作一般分类的说法
senses.example: Old electrical appliances use far more power.
senses.exampleCN: 旧家用电器耗电多得多。
senses.why: A whole class of goods is sorted by what drives them, so the classifying adjective takes the -al form.
senses.whyCN: 一整类商品按驱动方式分类，于是这个分类形容词采用了 -al 形式。

senses.title: Of the theory of electricity
senses.definition: relating to the scientific study of electricity and its properties
senses.definitionCN: 指对电及其性质的科学理论研究
senses.example: The paper compares the electrical properties of the two metals.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文比较了两种金属的电学性质。
senses.why: Properties belong to the science rather than to a machine, so the academic sense also takes -al.
senses.whyCN: 性质属于科学而不属于某台机器，所以学术义也用 -al 形式。

items.en: Seventeenth-century science coined electricus for the force amber shows.
items.cn: 十七世纪科学造出 electricus，指琥珀所显现的那股力。

items.en: English took the adjective and used it for bodies that attract and repel.
items.cn: 英语借入这个形容词，用于相互吸引与排斥的物体。

items.en: The -al form was added to speak of the whole field rather than one object.
items.cn: 加上 -al 的形式用来谈整个领域，而不是单个物体。

items.en: Engineering, wiring and appliances settled into the -al branch, leaving electric for the vivid and the specific.
items.cn: 工程、布线与家电固定在 -al 这一支，把 electric 留给更具体、更生动的用法。

senses.title: The energy of moving charges
senses.definition: the energy produced by the movement of electric charges, which can light a lamp or drive a machine
senses.definitionCN: 由电荷运动产生的能量，可以点灯或驱动机器
senses.example: Copper wire carries electricity well.
senses.exampleCN: 铜线导电性能很好。
senses.why: The -ity ending turns the adjective electric into a noun of quality, and that quality is the energy a charged body holds.
senses.whyCN: -ity 词尾把形容词 electric 变成表性质的名词，而带电物体所持有的那种性质就是这股能量。

senses.title: A supply to buildings
senses.definition: the supply of electric power through wires to homes, offices and streets
senses.definitionCN: 通过电线输送到住宅、办公室与街道的电力
senses.example: The storm cut off the electricity to the whole village.
senses.exampleCN: 这场暴风雨切断了整个村子的供电。
senses.why: Once the energy is piped into buildings, the abstract force becomes a service that can be billed or cut off.
senses.whyCN: 这股能量一旦被送进建筑，抽象的力量就变成一项能开账单、也能被切断的服务。

senses.title: The science of the force
senses.definition: the branch of physics that studies electric charge, current and their effects
senses.definitionCN: 研究电荷、电流及其效应的物理学分支
senses.example: He is reading a history of electricity.
senses.exampleCN: 他正在读一部电学史。
senses.why: A named force needs a science, and English let the same noun do both jobs instead of coining a separate term.
senses.whyCN: 一股被命名的力需要一门科学，而英语让同一个名词兼做两件事，没有另造新词。

senses.title: A charged atmosphere
senses.definition: a feeling of tense excitement that seems to fill a room or a crowd
senses.definitionCN: 仿佛充满整个房间或人群的紧张兴奋感
senses.example: There was electricity in the air before the concert.
senses.exampleCN: 音乐会开始前，空气里满是紧张兴奋的气氛。
senses.why: A charged body makes hair stand up, and a charged room makes people tense, so the physical charge lends its name to excitement.
senses.whyCN: 带电的物体会让汗毛竖起，带电的房间会让人紧绷，于是物理的电荷把名字借给了兴奋感。

intro.en: Electricity is electric plus the Latin noun ending -ity; electric itself goes back through Latin electrum to Greek elektron, amber, whose rubbed surface first showed attraction.
intro.cn: electricity 是 electric 加拉丁语名词词尾 -ity；electric 本身经拉丁语 electrum 上溯到希腊语 elektron（琥珀），琥珀摩擦后的表面最先显现出吸引现象。

items.en: Elektron meant amber, the resin that crackles and attracts when rubbed.
items.cn: elektron 意为「琥珀」，这种树脂摩擦后会噼啪作响并吸引碎屑。

items.en: Latin took the word as electrum, naming both amber and a pale gold-silver alloy.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入作 electrum，既指琥珀，也指一种淡金色的金银合金。

items.en: Seventeenth-century experimenters coined electricus for bodies that attract and repel after rubbing.
items.cn: 十七世纪的实验者造出 electricus，指摩擦后能吸引与排斥的物体。

items.en: English borrowed the adjective and used it for the force as well as the objects.
items.cn: 英语借入这个形容词，既用于物体，也用于那股力。

items.en: Adding -ity produced a noun for the force itself, recorded in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 加上 -ity 造出指这股力本身的名词，十七世纪已有记载。

items.en: The utility sense and the metaphor of a charged room grew out of the same noun.
items.cn: 供电义与「带电房间」的比喻，都是从同一个名词里长出来的。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the electricity family; the near-meaning group separates the energy from power, current and energy itself.
note.cn: 形近组收 electricity 词族；近义组把这份「电」与 power、current、energy 区分开。

entries.definition: Of the force itself, or of one device that runs on it.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「电的；用电的」，多指力量本身或单个器具。

entries.definition: Of electricity as a system of wiring and engineering.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「电气的」，指布线与工程意义上的电。

entries.definition: A tradesperson who installs and repairs wiring.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「电工」。

entries.definition: To charge with electricity, or to thrill someone.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使通电；使震惊」。

entries.definition: The supply of energy to a building, often used for electricity in the home.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「电力、动力」，常用来指住宅的供电。

entries.definition: The flow of charge through a wire; a rate, not the energy itself.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「电流」，指电荷在导线中的流动，是速率而非能量本身。

entries.definition: The general capacity to do work, of which electricity is one form.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「能量」，是做功的一般能力，电只是其中一种形式。

entries.definition: The plain word for the feeling that the charged metaphor describes.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「兴奋」，是那种带电气氛所比喻的直白说法。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from amber rubbed in the dark and follow the spark into wires, bills and a tense room.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从黑暗中摩擦的琥珀出发，让火花一路走进电线、电费单与紧绷的房间。

normal.en: Electric plus -ity: the quality of being electric becomes a substance you can bill.
normal.cn: electric 加 -ity：带电的性质变成一种能开账单的东西。

normal.en: Amber rubbed on wool is the first experiment behind the word.
normal.cn: 琥珀在羊毛上摩擦，是这个词背后最早的那个实验。

normal.en: Static electricity clings; current electricity flows.
normal.cn: static electricity 停在原地；current electricity 沿导线流动。

normal.en: Cut off the electricity and the whole village goes dark.
normal.cn: 切断 electricity，整个村子就黑了。

normal.en: A room full of electricity is a room where nobody can sit still.
normal.cn: 满是 electricity 的房间，就是没人坐得住的那个房间。

abstract.en: Picture a copper wire as a river, with charge instead of water.
abstract.cn: 把铜线想成一条河，河里流的不是水，而是电荷。

abstract.en: The same river can be a science, a bill, or a mood.
abstract.cn: 同一条河可以是一门科学、一张账单，也可以是一种情绪。

abstract.en: Electricity is a name for a force that behaves like a fluid and a feeling.
abstract.cn: electricity 是一股力的名字，它既像流体，又像情绪。

examples.en: Copper wire carries electricity well.
examples.cn: 铜线导电性能很好。

examples.en: The storm cut off the electricity to the whole village.
examples.cn: 这场暴风雨切断了整个村子的供电。

examples.en: There was electricity in the air before the concert.
examples.cn: 音乐会开始前，空气里满是紧张兴奋的气氛。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一来克锤西提」——按下开关，铜线里那股劲儿立刻冲到灯泡里

root: 由 electric 加拉丁语名词词尾 -ity 构成；electric 源自希腊语 elektron「琥珀」，经拉丁语 electrum 与近代拉丁语 electricus 而来。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses of electricity: the energy itself, the supply to buildings, the science that studies it, and the metaphor of a tense room.
sensesIntro.cn: electricity 的四个义项：能量本身、输送到建筑的供电、研究它的学科，以及「紧绷房间」的比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a filament flaring inside a bulb as current races along a copper wire.
core.cn: 核心意象：电流沿铜线奔涌，灯泡里的细丝骤然发亮。

branches.en: THE ENERGY: charge in motion, measured and used.
branches.cn: 能量线：运动中的电荷，被计量、被使用。

branches.en: THE SUPPLY: the same energy delivered as a service.
branches.cn: 供给线：同一股能量以服务的形式送到门口。

branches.en: THE SCIENCE: the force turned into an object of study.
branches.cn: 学科线：这股力变成被研究的对象。

branches.en: THE FEELING: a charged room borrows the physical word.
branches.cn: 情绪线：带电的房间借用了这个物理词。

branches.en: THE CURRENT: what flows in the wire is what arrives at the socket.
branches.cn: 电流线：导线里流动的东西，正是插座里到达的东西。

intro.en: Electricity is electric plus the Latin noun ending -ity; the stem behind it is the Greek word for amber.
intro.cn: electricity 是 electric 加拉丁语名词词尾 -ity；它背后的词干是希腊语里表示「琥珀」的词。

latinIntro.en: Greek elektron and Latin electrum are recorded; electricus and electricity were coined later by scientists.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 elektron 与拉丁语 electrum 有记录；electricus 与 electricity 是后来由科学家造出的。

items.example: It carried the word into Latin.
items.exampleCN: 它把这个词带入拉丁语。

items.example: It was coined in the seventeenth century.
It is the base of the whole family.

definition_zh: 电子；（作定语）电子的；价电子
definition_en: a very small particle with a negative charge that moves around the nucleus of an atom
core_image: 原子中心一颗核，外面几个极小的光点绕着它飞
scene: 示波管里一束细线被磁场轻轻推开，屏幕上留下弯曲的轨迹。A beam of electrons bends as it passes the magnet.
sceneCN: 这里 electron 是「电子」（第 1 个义项：带负电的亚原子粒子）；句意是一束电子经过磁铁时发生了偏转。

pos.zh: 名词：电子；价电子；（作定语）电子的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ic 构成，义为「电子的；电子设备的」
由 electronic 加 -s 构成，义为「电子学；电子器件」
由本词与 negative 复合，义为「电负性的」

senses.title: The negative particle
senses.definition: a stable subatomic particle with a negative charge that orbits the nucleus of an atom
senses.definitionCN: 一种带负电、绕原子核运动的稳定亚原子粒子
senses.example: An electron carries a negative charge.
senses.exampleCN: 一个电子带负电荷。
senses.why: When physicists needed a name for the tiny carrier of charge, they reached back to the amber root that had named the force.
senses.whyCN: 物理学家要给电荷的微小载体命名时，又回到了当初为这股力命名的「琥珀」词根。

senses.title: Before a noun as a tool
senses.definition: used before another noun for devices or beams that steer electrons, as in electron microscope
senses.definitionCN: 放在另一名词前，指操控电子束的装置，如电子显微镜
senses.example: The lab bought a new electron microscope.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室买了一台新的电子显微镜。
senses.why: The particle became a measuring tool, so its name moved in front of the instrument it drives.
senses.whyCN: 这个粒子成了测量工具，于是它的名字挪到了由它驱动的仪器前面。

senses.title: The electron in a bond
senses.definition: an outer electron that an atom shares or trades when it forms a chemical bond
senses.definitionCN: 原子成键时交出或共享的外层电子
senses.example: Each carbon atom shares four electrons.
senses.exampleCN: 每个碳原子共享四个电子。
senses.why: Chemistry counts only the outermost electrons when it explains bonds, and each one keeps the same name.
senses.whyCN: 化学在解释成键时只数最外层电子，而每一个仍用同一个名字。

intro.en: Electron revives a Greek word for amber; the modern particle name was proposed at the end of the nineteenth century and confirmed when the particle itself was found.
intro.cn: electron 复活了希腊语里表示「琥珀」的词；这个现代粒子名在十九世纪末被提出，并在粒子本身被发现后得到确认。

items.en: Elektron meant amber, and later also the pale alloy that looked like it.
items.cn: elektron 意为「琥珀」，后来也指外观相似的淡色合金。

items.en: Latin kept the word as electrum and passed the root into the science of charge.
items.cn: 拉丁语保留作 electrum，并把这个词根传进了研究电荷的科学。

items.en: The adjective electric made the root familiar before the particle had a name.
items.cn: 在粒子得名之前，形容词 electric 已让这个词根为人熟悉。

items.en: The physicist Stoney proposed electron as the name of a unit of charge.
items.cn: 物理学家斯通尼提议用 electron 作为电荷单位的名称。

items.en: Thomson's experiments showed that a real particle carried that charge.
items.cn: 汤姆孙的实验证明真的有一种粒子携带这份电荷。

items.en: The name settled on the particle, and the suffix -ic later produced electronic.
items.cn: 这个名字最终固定给了粒子，而 -ic 词尾后来造出了 electronic。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the electric family; the near-meaning group sorts the atom's particles and the charge they carry.
note.cn: 形近组收 electric 词族；近义组区分原子里的几种粒子以及它们携带的电荷。

entries.definition: Of the force, or of a device driven by it.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「电的；用电的」。

entries.definition: Working by controlling electrons in circuits.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「电子的」，靠控制电路中的电子工作。

entries.definition: The science of electron control, or the circuits themselves.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「电子学；电子器件」。

entries.definition: The energy of moving charges.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「电；电力」。

entries.definition: A particle in the nucleus with a positive charge; equal and opposite to the electron.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「质子」，位于核内、带正电，与电子电量相等、符号相反。

entries.definition: A particle in the nucleus with no charge at all.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「中子」，位于核内，不带电。

entries.definition: An atom that has gained or lost electrons and so carries a charge.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「离子」，是得失电子后带电的原子。

entries.definition: The property itself that the electron carries, not the particle.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「电荷」，是电子所携带的性质，而不是粒子本身。

normalIntro.en: These hooks shrink the amber word down to a point of charge and then hand it to microscopes and bonds.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子把「琥珀」那个词缩小成一个电荷点，再交给显微镜与化学键。

normal.en: Electron is the smallest piece of the amber story.
normal.cn: electron 是琥珀这个故事里最小的一块。

normal.en: Protons sit in the middle; electrons run around them.
normal.cn: 质子坐在正中，电子绕着它们跑。

normal.en: An electron microscope sees with particles, not with light.
normal.cn: 电子显微镜用粒子看东西，而不是用光。

normal.en: Bonds are electron deals: share one, give one away.
normal.cn: 化学键就是电子的交易：共享一个，或送走一个。

normal.en: Electric is the field; electron is the smallest worker in it.
normal.cn: electric 是整片场；electron 是场里最小的那个工人。

abstract.en: Picture a nucleus as a lit lamp and electrons as moths circling it.
abstract.cn: 把原子核想成一盏亮着的灯，电子就是绕着它飞的蛾子。

abstract.en: The same word names one particle and a whole technology built on it.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既命名一种粒子，也命名建立在它之上的整套技术。

abstract.en: Electron is a point of charge; everything electronic is that point multiplied.
abstract.cn: electron 是一个电荷点；一切 electronic 的东西都是这个点的千百倍复制。

examples.en: An electron carries a negative charge.
examples.cn: 一个电子带负电荷。

examples.en: A beam of electrons bends as it passes the magnet.
examples.cn: 一束电子经过磁铁时发生了偏转。

examples.en: Each carbon atom shares four electrons.
examples.cn: 每个碳原子共享四个电子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一颗来克胀」——原子外那颗极小的光点，绕一圈又一圈

root: 源自希腊语 elektron「琥珀」，经拉丁语 electrum 进入英语的科学词汇；十九世纪末被用来命名带负电的粒子。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of electron: the particle, the word used before an instrument's name, and the outer electron counted in bonds.
sensesIntro.cn: electron 的三个义项：粒子本身、放在仪器名前作定语，以及成键时被计数的外层电子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small bright point circling a heavy nucleus.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个明亮的小点绕着重核旋转。

branches.en: THE PARTICLE: the carrier of negative charge.
branches.cn: 粒子线：负电荷的载体。

branches.en: THE TOOL: the same name in front of an instrument.
branches.cn: 工具线：同一个名字被放在仪器前面。

branches.en: THE BOND: the outer electron that chemistry counts.
branches.cn: 成键线：化学所数的外层电子。

branches.en: THE OUTERMOST: the electron that is shared is still the same particle.
branches.cn: 最外层线：被共享的那个电子仍然是同一种粒子。

branches.en: THE BEAM: many electrons lined up become an instrument.
branches.cn: 电子束线：许多电子排齐，就成了一件仪器。

intro.en: Electron is built on the amber root plus the Greek noun ending -on; the same root feeds electric and electronic.
intro.cn: electron 用「琥珀」词根加希腊语名词词尾 -on 构成；同一个词根还养出 electric 与 electronic。

latinIntro.en: Greek elektron and Latin electrum are the recorded forms; electron as a particle name is modern.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 elektron 与拉丁语 electrum 是有记录的形式；作为粒子名的 electron 属于现代造词。

items.example: It names the substance that started it all.
items.exampleCN: 它命名了这一切的起点物质。

items.example: It passed the root on to Latin.
items.exampleCN: 它把这个词根传给拉丁语。
它让这个词根为人熟悉。
它命名一种亚原子粒子。

items.example: It appears in electron and proton.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 electron 与 proton 中。

definition_zh: 电子的；电子设备的；电子化的；电子音乐的；电子学的
definition_en: working by controlling the flow of electrons in circuits, using computer or network technology, made with synthesizers, or relating to the science of electronics
core_image: 电路板上密布芯片与细如发丝的走线，指示灯一闪一闪
scene: 超市收银台前，顾客把手机贴在读卡器上，滴一声就完成了付款。Most shops now accept electronic payment.
sceneCN: 这里 electronic 是「电子化的、用电子手段完成的」（第 2 个义项：借助计算机与网络技术）；句意是多数商店现在都接受电子支付。

pos.zh: 形容词：电子的；电子设备的；电子化的；电子音乐的；电子学的

forms.label: 比较级（形容词，多音节用 more）
最高级（形容词，多音节用 most）

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉 -ic 得到，义为「电子」
由本词加 -s 构成，义为「电子学；电子器件」

由本词加 -ian 构成，义为「电子工程师」

senses.title: Working through circuits
senses.titleCN: 电子的；靠电子电路工作的
senses.definition: operating by controlling the movement of electrons through circuits such as transistors and chips
senses.definitionCN: 通过控制电子在晶体管、芯片等电路中流动来工作
senses.example: The lab is testing a new electronic circuit.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室正在测试一块新的电子电路。
senses.why: The suffix -ic turns the particle name into an adjective, so the word describes anything that works by steering electrons.
senses.whyCN: -ic 词尾把粒子名变成形容词，于是这个词形容一切靠操控电子来工作的东西。

senses.title: Done by computer or network
senses.titleCN: 电子化的；用电子手段完成的
senses.definition: carried out using computers, networks or digital systems rather than paper or face-to-face contact
senses.definitionCN: 借助计算机、网络或数字系统完成，而不是纸面或面对面
senses.example: Most shops now accept electronic payment.
senses.exampleCN: 多数商店现在都接受电子支付。
senses.why: Once a whole transaction runs through chips and networks, the device adjective spreads to the activity itself.
senses.whyCN: 当一笔交易整个跑在芯片与网络上，指设备的形容词就扩展到了活动本身。

senses.title: Made with synthesizers
senses.definition: of music produced with synthesizers, samplers and other electronic instruments
senses.definitionCN: 用合成器、采样器及其他电子乐器制作的音乐
senses.example: She writes electronic music on a laptop.
senses.exampleCN: 她在笔记本电脑上写电子音乐。
senses.why: The instruments are the style, so the adjective naming the technology ended up naming a whole genre.
senses.whyCN: 乐器就是风格本身，于是命名这项技术的形容词最后成了一个音乐流派的名称。

senses.title: Of the science of electronics
senses.definition: relating to electronics as a branch of engineering and physics
senses.definitionCN: 指作为工程学与物理学分支的电子学
senses.example: He teaches electronic engineering.
senses.exampleCN: 他教电子工程。
senses.why: The field that studies these circuits needed a name, and the adjective before engineering supplied it.
senses.whyCN: 研究这些电路的那门学科需要名字，而 engineering 前面的这个形容词正好提供了它。

intro.en: Electronic is electron plus -ic, coined once the particle had been found; the root itself is the Greek word for amber.
intro.cn: electronic 是 electron 加 -ic，在粒子被发现之后才造出；而这个词根本身是希腊语里的「琥珀」。

items.en: Elektron named amber, whose rubbed surface first showed attraction.
items.cn: elektron 指琥珀，摩擦后的表面最先显现出吸引现象。

items.en: Latin kept electrum for amber and passed the root into modern science.
items.cn: 拉丁语保留 electrum 表示琥珀，并把这个词根传进近代科学。

items.en: The particle name electron gave the family a solid centre.
items.cn: 粒子名 electron 为这个词族提供了坚实的中心。

items.en: Valves and then transistors made a new adjective necessary for circuits.
items.cn: 电子管以及后来的晶体管，使指电路的形容词成为必需。

items.en: The -ic form covered devices, then transactions, then music.
items.cn: 加 -ic 的形式先指设备，再指交易，最后指音乐。

items.en: Electronic now names a whole layer of daily life built on chips.
items.cn: 如今 electronic 命名了建立在芯片之上的整整一层日常生活。

note.en: The look-alike group lines up the electric family; the near-meaning group separates electronic from electric, digital and electrical.
note.cn: 形近组排开 electric 词族；近义组区分 electronic 与 electric、digital、electrical。

entries.definition: The negative particle that these circuits control.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「电子」，正是这些电路所控制的粒子。

entries.definition: The science of such circuits, or the circuits as goods.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「电子学」，也指作为商品的电子器件。

entries.definition: By electronic means.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「用电子方式地」。

entries.definition: Of wiring and power systems rather than of chips.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「电气的」，指布线供电系统而非芯片。

entries.definition: Driven by electricity in the plain sense, as a kettle or a motor.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「用电的」，指水壶、马达这类普通用电的东西。

entries.definition: Stored as numbers; overlaps the network sense but says nothing about circuits.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「数字的」，与网络义重叠，但不涉及电路。

entries.definition: Belonging to the power system, a wider and older field.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「电气的」，属于更宽、更早的电力领域。

entries.definition: Run by machines; close to the transaction sense but not tied to chips.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「自动化的」，接近交易义，但不限于芯片。

normalIntro.en: These hooks walk from a single electron to a chip, then to a payment, a track and a degree.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从一个电子走到一块芯片，再走到一笔支付、一首曲子与一个学位。

normal.en: One electron is a particle; electronic is a whole way of working.
normal.cn: 一个电子是粒子；electronic 则是一整套工作方式。

normal.en: Electric kettles heat; electronic devices decide.
normal.cn: electric 水壶负责加热；electronic 设备负责判断。

normal.en: Electronic mail is mail without paper.
normal.cn: electronic mail 就是没有纸的邮件。

normal.en: Electronic music is music without a visible instrument.
normal.cn: electronic music 就是看不见乐器的音乐。

normal.en: A chip is a city of electrons with traffic rules.
normal.cn: 一块芯片就是一座有交通规则的电子之城。

abstract.en: Picture a circuit board as an aerial map of a small city at night.
abstract.cn: 把电路板想成夜里一座小城市的航拍图。

abstract.en: Electrons are the traffic; the chip is the road plan.
abstract.cn: 电子是车流；芯片是道路规划。

abstract.en: Electronic is what happens when the smallest particle is put in charge of the biggest systems.
abstract.cn: electronic 就是最小的粒子掌管最大系统时发生的事。

examples.en: The lab is testing a new electronic circuit.
examples.cn: 实验室正在测试一块新的电子电路。

examples.en: Most shops now accept electronic payment.
examples.cn: 多数商店现在都接受电子支付。

examples.en: She writes electronic music on a laptop.
examples.cn: 她在笔记本电脑上写电子音乐。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一颗来克胀尼克」——芯片上密密麻麻的走线一起闪，机器就活了

root: 由 electron 加形容词词尾 -ic 构成；electron 源自希腊语 elektron「琥珀」，经拉丁语 electrum 进入英语科学词汇。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses of electronic: circuits, computer-based activities, synth music, and the engineering field.
sensesIntro.cn: electronic 的四个义项：电子电路、依托计算机的活动、合成器音乐，以及电子工程学科。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chip with hair-thin tracks and a blinking indicator light.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块芯片，走线细如发丝，指示灯一闪一闪。

branches.en: THE CIRCUIT: electrons steered by transistors and chips.
branches.cn: 电路线：由晶体管与芯片操控的电子。

branches.en: THE TRANSACTION: money and mail moved through networks.
branches.cn: 交易线：透过网络转移的钱与邮件。

branches.en: THE GENRE: a style named after its instruments.
branches.cn: 流派线：以乐器命名的一种音乐风格。

branches.en: THE FIELD: the engineering that designs the circuits.
branches.cn: 学科线：设计这些电路的工程学。

branches.en: THE CHIP: every paperless payment is a chip doing arithmetic.
branches.cn: 芯片线：每一笔无纸支付，都是芯片在做算术。

intro.en: Electronic is electron with the adjective suffix -ic; the root behind both is the Greek word for amber.
intro.cn: electronic 是 electron 加形容词词尾 -ic；两者背后的词根都是希腊语的「琥珀」。

latinIntro.en: Greek elektron and Latin electrum are the older recorded forms; electron and electronic are modern coinages.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 elektron 与拉丁语 electrum 是较早的有记录形式；electron 与 electronic 都是现代造词。

items.example: It is the root of the whole family.
It supplies the stem of this word.
items.exampleCN: 它提供了这个词的词干。

derivatives.zh: 电子
电子学；电子器件
用电子方式地
电子工程师

definition_zh: 优雅的；高雅的；雅致的；简洁精妙的
definition_en: graceful and stylish in appearance or manner, pleasingly simple in design, or neat and clever as a solution
core_image: 一个人穿着剪裁利落的深色长裙，走过大厅时几乎不发出声音
scene: 评审会上，年轻工程师在白板上写下三行公式，难题当场解开。Her elegant proof took only three lines.
sceneCN: 这里 elegant 是「（方案）简洁精妙的」（第 3 个义项：以最少的步骤漂亮地解决问题）；句意是她的证明只用了三行。

pos.zh: 形容词：优雅的；高雅的；雅致的；简洁精妙的

forms.label: 比较级（形容词，多音节用 more）
最高级（形容词，多音节用 most）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ance 构成，义为「优雅；雅致；简洁」
由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「优雅地；简洁地」
由本词加否定前缀 in- 构成，义为「不雅的；笨拙的」

senses.title: Graceful in manner
senses.definition: moving, speaking or behaving with natural grace and good taste
senses.definitionCN: 举止、言谈自然而得体，显出良好的品味
senses.example: She gave an elegant bow at the end of the performance.
senses.exampleCN: 演出结束时，她优雅地鞠了一躬。
senses.why: Latin elegans first meant choosy and tasteful, and a person who chooses well in movement looks graceful.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 elegans 最初意为「挑剔的、有品味的」，而在举止上选得恰到好处的人，看上去就优雅。

senses.title: Stylish and simple in design
senses.definition: pleasingly simple and well proportioned, without anything extra
senses.definitionCN: 简洁而比例匀称，没有任何多余之物
senses.example: The room was simple but elegant.
senses.exampleCN: 这个房间简单却很雅致。
senses.why: Good taste removes rather than adds, so the same word praises a design for what it leaves out.
senses.whyCN: 好品味是删而不是加，于是同一个词用「省掉了什么」来称赞一件设计。

senses.title: Neat and clever as a solution
senses.definition: of a proof, method or solution, achieved in few steps with surprising neatness
senses.definitionCN: 指证明、方法或方案步骤极少却出人意料地漂亮
senses.example: Her elegant proof took only three lines.
senses.exampleCN: 她的证明只用了三行。
senses.why: A proof that wastes nothing is admired the way a graceful body is, so the aesthetic word moved into mathematics.
senses.whyCN: 一条不浪费任何步骤的证明，会被像欣赏优雅身姿那样欣赏，于是这个审美词走进了数学。

intro.en: Elegant comes from Latin elegans, a word for tasteful and choosy, built on eligere, to pick out; it reached English through French.
intro.cn: elegant 来自拉丁语 elegans，意为「有品味的、会挑选的」，其根是 eligere（挑出）；它经法语进入英语。

items.en: Eligere meant to pick out or choose, from ex plus legere, to gather.
items.cn: eligere 意为「挑出、选择」，由 ex 加 legere（收取）构成。

items.en: The participle elegans described someone who chooses well and so has fine taste.
items.cn: 分词 elegans 形容一个人会挑选，因而品味出众。

items.en: French borrowed the word for refined and handsome.
items.cn: 法语借入这个词，表示「精致的、俊雅的」。

items.en: English took it for manners and dress that show good taste.
items.cn: 英语借入它，指表现出好品味的举止与衣着。

items.en: Design and mathematics extended it to anything done with the fewest parts.
items.cn: 设计与数学把它扩展到一切「用最少部件完成」的事物上。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps elegance and its false friend elegy apart; the near-meaning group sorts grace, style and refinement.
note.cn: 形近组把 elegance 与易混的 elegy 分开；近义组区分 grace、style 与 refinement。

entries.definition: The quality of being elegant; the noun behind the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「优雅；雅致；简洁」，是本词的派生名词。

entries.definition: In an elegant manner.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「优雅地；简洁地」。

entries.definition: Lacking grace or taste; the in- prefix reverses the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不雅的；笨拙的」，由 in- 否定本词。

entries.definition: A mournful poem; it looks close but has a different root and means sorrow.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「挽歌」，形近但词源不同，意思是哀悼。

entries.definition: Smooth and flowing in movement; about the body rather than taste.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「优美的」，强调动作流畅，而非品味。

entries.definition: Fashionable and striking; more about current trend than restraint.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「时髦的」，更看重当下潮流而非克制。

entries.definition: Polished by culture and training; the result of long cultivation.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有修养的、精炼的」，是长期教养的结果。

entries.definition: Neat and well dressed, or clever; broader and more casual.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「整洁漂亮的；聪明的」，更宽泛也更口语。

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie the word to choosing well, then let that taste spread from a person to a room to a proof.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子把词义系在「会挑」上，再让这份品味从人扩到房间、再到一条证明。

normal.en: Elegant and elect share the Latin verb to choose.
normal.cn: elegant 与 elect 共用一个拉丁语动词，意思是「挑选」。

normal.en: Good taste is mostly what you leave out.
normal.cn: 好品味多半在于你省掉了什么。

normal.en: An elegant dress has no extra line on it.
normal.cn: 一件 elegant 的连衣裙，身上没有多余的一道线。

normal.en: An elegant proof has no extra step in it.
normal.cn: 一条 elegant 的证明，里面没有多余的一步。

normal.en: Elegy is a funeral song; elegant is good taste. Keep them apart.
normal.cn: elegy 是挽歌，elegant 是好品味，别把两者混在一起。

abstract.en: Picture a hand picking one fruit from a full basket, without hesitating.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手从满篮水果里毫不犹豫地挑出一只。

abstract.en: Choice made clean is what the eye calls beautiful.
abstract.cn: 干净利落的选择，眼睛就称之为美。

abstract.en: Elegant is the shape of a decision that needed nothing more.
abstract.cn: elegant 是一个「再不需要多一点」的决定所呈现的形状。

examples.en: She gave an elegant bow at the end of the performance.
examples.cn: 演出结束时，她优雅地鞠了一躬。

examples.en: The room was simple but elegant.
examples.cn: 这个房间简单却很雅致。

examples.en: Her elegant proof took only three lines.
examples.cn: 她的证明只用了三行。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「艾勒甘」——挑衣服只挑一件，穿上就再不用添任何配饰

root: 源自拉丁语 elegans「有品味的、会挑选的」，其根为 eligere（挑出，由 ex + legere 构成），经法语 élégant 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of elegant: graceful bearing, tasteful simplicity in design, and neatness in a proof or solution.
sensesIntro.cn: elegant 的三个义项：优雅的举止、设计上的雅致简洁，以及证明或方案上的简洁精妙。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand choosing one perfect fruit from a full basket.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手从满篮水果中挑出一只最合适的。

branches.en: THE BEARING: a person whose movements show good choice.
branches.cn: 举止线：动作里显出好眼光的人。

branches.en: THE DESIGN: simplicity praised as good taste.
branches.cn: 设计线：被当作好品味来称赞的简洁。

branches.en: THE PROOF: the same restraint applied to reasoning.
branches.cn: 证明线：同样的克制用在推理上。

branches.en: THE SPARE: what is left out is the compliment.
branches.cn: 删减线：省掉的部分才是称赞所在。

branches.en: THE SURFACE: a graceful body and a graceful room are read the same way.
branches.cn: 外观线：优雅的身姿与雅致的房间，读法完全相同。

intro.en: Elegant is the Latin participle elegans, from eligere, to pick out; the -ant ending is the mark of that participle.
intro.cn: elegant 就是拉丁语分词 elegans，出自 eligere（挑出）；-ant 词尾正是这个分词的标记。

latinIntro.en: Eligere and elegans are recorded Latin forms; English took the word through French rather than directly.
latinIntro.cn: eligere 与 elegans 都是有记录的拉丁语形式；英语是经法语而非直接借入这个词的。

items.example: It supplies the root of the word.
items.exampleCN: 它提供了这个词的词根。

items.example: It is the parent of elegans.

items.meaningCN: 处于某种状态或正在做

优雅地；简洁地
